The Melusines.heading: Daughters of the Slain Beast Elynas
paragraphs: Unique to the nation of Fontaine, the Melusines are a gentle, subterranean race of small, amphibious humanoid beings possessing pastel skin, rabbit-like antenna ears, and short tails. Despite their cute and peaceful appearance, their biological origin is rooted in the darkest tragedy of the Cataclysm: they were born from the severed flesh, blood, and internal splinters of Elynas, the colossal abyssal leviathan created by the alchemist Rhinedottir.

Five hundred years ago, after Elynas fell dead in the waters of the Beryl Region, its titanic corpse began undergoing a gentle transformation over decades. From the internal fractures and crystalline wounds within its petrified heart, the first Melusine sisters—such as Sigewinne, Carole, and Sedene—emerged into consciousness, hearing the benevolent, loving voice of their 'Father' Elynas guiding them to live happily in the world.

The Melusines.heading: Perception Beyond Human Senses
paragraphs: Melusines perceive reality in a manner fundamentally alien to human biology. Their eyesight does not register the electromagnetic spectrum in the same way; instead, they see the world through subtle gradients of color that reflect emotional auras, metaphysical residue, and elemental intent. A human criminal might look physically pristine, but to a Melusine, they might appear surrounded by a foul, dark green mist of guilt and deceit.

Because of this extraordinary sensory capability and their natural ability to breathe underwater indefinitely, Melusines possess an unparalleled talent for forensic investigation, mechanical appraisal, and underwater exploration. The famous Marechaussee Phantom—Fontaine's elite investigative detective force—relies heavily on Melusine detectives to uncover clues and solve crimes that completely baffle human officers.

The Melusines.heading: The Tragedy of Carole and Neuvillette's Protection
paragraphs: When the Melusines first ventured out of Merusea Village into human society four hundred years ago, they were met with cruel xenophobia and suspicion from Fontaine's human aristocracy, who feared them as abyssal monsters. The hostility culminated in the heartbreak of Carole, a sweet Melusine who was framed in a political conspiracy and chose to take her own life to prevent human civil unrest.

Chief Justice Neuvillette, who had welcomed the Melusines as his own kin and cherished their purity of heart, was deeply wounded by Carole's death. Neuvillette enacted strict, unyielding laws granting Melusines full civil equality, criminalizing anti-Melusine discrimination, and requiring all citizens to address them with the respectful gender-neutral pronoun 'elle' in official Fontaine law. Under his steadfast protection, Melusines gradually integrated into every stratum of Fontaine society.

The Melusines.heading: Beloved Citizens of the Court
paragraphs: Today, Melusines are beloved and respected across Fontaine. They operate the steam-powered Clementine and Navia aquabus lines, serve as trusted court clerks, conduct scientific research, and provide medical care, with Sigewinne serving as the compassionate Head Nurse of the Fortress of Meropide.
Their gentle presence serves as a living testament to redemption: that even from the shattered remains of an abyssal monster, life of supreme kindness, innocence, and beauty can be born.

Natlan’s Saurians.heading: The Noble Kin of the Dragon Realm
paragraphs: Across the volcanic canyons, thermal springs, and canopy forests of Natlan, human warriors live alongside Saurians—the evolutionary descendants of the ancient dragon race that ruled Teyvat before the dawn of humanity. While dragons in other nations are often solitary, ancient leviathans, Natlan's Saurians have adapted over millennia to live in joyful, intimate symbiosis with the Six Great Human Tribes.

Saurians are not treated as domestic cattle or disposable war mounts; they are regarded as family, brothers-in-arms, and cultural kin. A Natlan child often grows up alongside a Saurian whelp, forging a lifelong bond of emotional resonance that enables them to coordinate with extraordinary precision in both peaceful daily chores and harrowing combat against the Abyss.

Natlan’s Saurians.heading: The Specialized Breeds of the Six Tribes
paragraphs: Through centuries of environmental adaptation, several distinct Saurian breeds evolved, each possessing specialized biomechanical abilities that match the territory of their human tribe partners:

• Tepetlisaur (Children of the Echoes): Armored, powerful terrestrial Saurians with subterranean claws that allow them to swim through solid rock and cliff faces as if it were water, unearthing precious minerals.
• Yumkasaur (Scions of the Canopy): Agile, arboreal Saurians that can ingest explosive flame berries and launch high-velocity grappling hooks from their mouths, swinging effortlessly across yawning canyon voids.
• Koholasaur (People of the Springs): Sleek, aquatic Saurians with fins that enable them to skim across liquid lava pools and rushing sea currents at blinding speeds, generating shockwaves on the water's surface.
• Qucusaur (Flower-Feather Clan): Feathered, majestic aerial Saurians that soar through the thermals of high volcanic peaks, carrying riders across immense sky distances.

Natlan’s Saurians.heading: The Art of Indwelling
paragraphs: Unique to Natlan is the spiritual ability known as 'Indwelling'—a mystical technique that allows a human warrior (and the Traveler) to project their consciousness into a wild or allied Saurian. When indwelling, the human's physical body dissolves temporarily into spirit, taking direct control of the Saurian's elemental anatomy.

Indwelling is not an act of mental domination; it is an act of shared spiritual consent rooted in the mutual harmony of dragon and human souls. Through indwelling, warriors experience the world through the Saurian's acute instincts, feeling the vibrations of the bedrock, the thermal currents of the air, or the fluid dynamics of hot springs.

Natlan’s Saurians.heading: Warriors of the Night Kingdom
paragraphs: In Natlan's desperate, eternal struggle against the Abyss, Saurians fight on the frontlines alongside human champions. When Abyssal incursions breach the borders, Saurian packs defend the tribes with ferocious loyalty, willingly laying down their lives to protect human infants and sacred tribal shrines.

Their souls, like those of mortal warriors, return to the Night Kingdom, remembered in the sacred songs of the land. In a world where dragons and gods have so often fought for dominance, Natlan's Saurians represent a radiant beacon of unity: the living proof that different species can walk hand-in-hand as equals.

The Skyfrost Nail.heading: The Pillar That Froze a Mountain Kingdom
paragraphs: Soaring atop the frozen, blizzard-whipped peak of Dragonspine sits the Skyfrost Nail, a colossal, glowing celestial monolith shattered into floating fragments around a swirling core of icy atmospheric power. For millennia, travelers in Mondstadt looked up at the frozen mountain with dread, believing the blizzard was natural.

However, ancient stone carvings and archaeological murals hidden throughout the mountain's subterranean chambers reveal a horrifying truth: Dragonspine was once a lush, verdant mountain kingdom named Sal Vindagnyr, blessed with gentle breezes, green valleys, and an immense Irminsul silver tree. Its prosperity was obliterated in an instant when Celestia dropped the Skyfrost Nail directly from the sky, shattering the mountain's climate into a perpetual, killing winter.

The Skyfrost Nail.heading: The Destruction of Sal Vindagnyr
paragraphs: When the Skyfrost Nail struck the mountain, the impact shattered the sacred Irminsul tree into petrified wooden shards, severed the local Ley Lines, and unleashed an unnatural blizzard that extinguished all agriculture within days. The princess of Sal Vindagnyr, gifted with prophetic visions, attempted to graft the dying tree with her tears and blood, but the cold proved absolute.

The champion knight Imunlaukr traveled into the outer world seeking a miraculous cure to save the kingdom, but by the time he returned, everyone—including the princess, the royal court, and the citizens—had frozen to death in their stone halls. Leaving behind only tragic stone murals and a bloodstained greatsword, Imunlaukr walked away, leaving the frozen kingdom to sleep beneath the snow for thousands of years.

The Skyfrost Nail.heading: The True Purpose: Celestial Quarantine
paragraphs: While early scholars believed the Skyfrost Nail was a weapon of divine punishment against mortals who sought to question the heavens, deeper archaeological discoveries in The Chasm, Sumeru's Mt. Damavand, and ancient Fontaine reveal a more complex, terrifying reality: the Celestial Nails are quarantine weapons.

Whenever a mortal kingdom began experimenting with Abyssal corruption, pierced the firmament, or suffered from leaking Forbidden Knowledge, Celestia deployed a Celestial Nail to crush the epicentre. The nails act as metaphysical anchors, pinning down the land to suppress the chaotic, reality-dissolving poison of the Abyss. Sal Vindagnyr's freezing was collateral damage in a brutal celestial campaign to keep Teyvat's elemental order from unraveling.

The Skyfrost Nail.heading: Awakening and Restoration
paragraphs: During the Traveler's exploration of Dragonspine alongside the Chief Alchemist Albedo, the three crystalline shards that broke off during the initial impact were thawed and restored to the central nail. As the monolith reassembled itself and rose into the sky above the summit, the suffocating blizzards around the peak began to clear, allowing sunlight to touch the frozen ruins for the first time in millennia.

The Skyfrost Nail stands as an unforgettable monument to Teyvat's tragic history: a testament to both the terrifying, ruthless power of the Heavenly Principles and the fragile beauty of mortal civilizations caught beneath heaven's hammer.

Sword of Narzissenkreuz.heading: The Holy Blade of the Ordo
paragraphs: The Sword of Narzissenkreuz is a legendary, radiant longsword forged through the profound esoteric research of the Narzissenkreuz Ordo—a secret society established in Fontaine five hundred years ago by brilliant orphans who sought to avert the prophesied Great Flood that threatened to dissolve the nation into the Primordial Sea.

Forged through the combined willpower, memories, and souls of Rene de Petrichor (the Master of the Ordo), Mary-Ann Guillotin, Jakob Ingold, and the Oceanid Ann, the blade is not merely steel; it is a metaphysical instrument designed to cut through the chains of preordained fate and harmonize the fundamental dualistic energies of Fontaine.

Sword of Narzissenkreuz.heading: The Mastery of Arkhe: Pneuma and Ousia
paragraphs: In gameplay and in lore, the Sword of Narzissenkreuz is unique among all weapons in Teyvat: it can freely alter its intrinsic Arkhe alignment between Pneuma (the golden, energetic principle) and Ousia (the dark, stable principle). Unlike other Fontaine characters whose Arkhe is fixed by their personal nature, the wielder of the Holy Blade can cleanse corrupted mechanical mechanisms and disrupt Abyssal energy with either polarity at will.

This duality mirrors the philosophy of the Narzissenkreuz Institute: that light and darkness, human reason and monstrous instinct, must be brought into conscious equilibrium rather than fighting an endless war of mutual destruction.

Sword of Narzissenkreuz.heading: Averting the Apocalypse of the Primordial Sea
paragraphs: Rene and Jakob foresaw that Fontaine would be wiped out when the Primordial Sea breached the surface. In their desperation, they resurrected ancient Remurian soul-transference rituals, attempting to dissolve humanity into a single collective consciousness within the Gestalt Tower to shield them from the coming apocalypse. However, in doing so, Rene became a mutated, monstrous amalgamation known as the 'Narzissenkreuz Master.'

It fell upon the Traveler, accompanied by the Oceanid Ann, the mechanical dog Seymour, and the painter Mamere, to enter the sunken Tower of Ipsissimus. Wielding the holy blade, the Traveler defeated the Narzissenkreuz Master, cutting away his twisted delusions of godhood while preserving the pure, original wish of the four orphans to protect their homeland.

Sword of Narzissenkreuz.heading: The Legacy of the Children of Fontaine
paragraphs: Following the resolution of the crisis, the Oceanid Ann and the remnants of Mary-Ann's soul stepped forward, laying their memories to rest in a peaceful dream garden. The Sword of Narzissenkreuz was entrusted permanently to the Traveler, standing as an enduring symbol of mortal love, courage, and the refusal to surrender to a cruel fate.
The story of the sword proves that even when prophecies seem immutable and divine decrees absolute, the sincere, united willpower of mortals can carve a path toward salvation.

Irminsul and the World’s Memories.heading: The Silver Tree at the Heart of the World
paragraphs: Deep within the subterranean roots of Teyvat lies Irminsul, the colossal, glowing silver-white world tree whose roots stretch across the entire continent, connecting every Ley Line, domain, and elemental vein in existence. Irminsul is not merely a botanical entity; it is the living neurological system and information database of Teyvat, recording every word spoken, every tear shed, every life lived, and every historical event that has ever occurred on the planet.

Whenever a mortal dies or an ancient god falls, their elemental energy and memories dissolve into the Ley Lines, gradually flowing back to the roots of Irminsul. Deities possessing deep resonance with the tree—such as the Dendro Archons Greater Lord Rukkhadevata and Lesser Lord Kusanali—can access its branches to consult past history, cure ecological blight, or speak through the minds of living beings.

Irminsul and the World’s Memories.heading: The Danger of Forbidden Knowledge
paragraphs: Because Irminsul is the information substrate of Teyvat, it is uniquely vulnerable to alien contaminants from outside the world. The deadliest of these is 'Forbidden Knowledge'—chaotic, corruptive information originating from the dark void of the Abyss. Unlike ordinary poisons, Forbidden Knowledge cannot be metabolized by Teyvat's elemental ecosystem; when it infects Irminsul, it causes the roots to rot, spawning the Withering in forests, the agonizing plague Eleazar in humans, and severe madness in gods.

Twice in history, Sumeru faced annihilation from Forbidden Knowledge: first during King Deshret's catastrophic experiments, and second during the Cataclysm 500 years ago. In both instances, divine sacrifice was required to prune the contaminated branches and quarantine the infection.

Irminsul and the World’s Memories.heading: Rewriting the Past: The Ultimate Memory Wipe
paragraphs: The most terrifying revelation regarding Irminsul was uncovered during the Sumeru Archon Quests: modifying a record in Irminsul does not merely alter historical books; it retroactively rewrites the conscious memories and recorded documents of every single person across Teyvat. Reality itself restructures its narrative to preserve causal continuity.

When Nahida erased Greater Lord Rukkhadevata from Irminsul, all texts, memories, and historical accounts across the seven nations changed in a single second: everyone believed Kusanali had been the sole Archon from the beginning. Similarly, when Scaramouche threw himself into Irminsul to erase his past sins, the world forgot the Balladeer, rewriting the tragedy of the Tatarasuna forge. However, because events cannot be undone—only forgotten—the physical consequences of the past remained intact.

Irminsul and the World’s Memories.heading: The Descender Exemption
paragraphs: Crucially, there is one supreme exception to Irminsul's reality manipulation: Descenders. Because beings such as the Traveler originate from outside Teyvat, their consciousness and memories are not tied to Irminsul's Ley Line network. When Rukkhadevata was erased, the Traveler was the only person on the entire continent who still remembered her name, her sacrifice, and her love.
This makes the Traveler the ultimate 'Witness' of Teyvat: the sole living archive who preserves the real, unvarnished history of the world, untainted by celestial edits or memory wipes.

The Three Moons.heading: The Celestial Maidens of the Primordial Sky
paragraphs: In the dawn of time, before the Archon War, before the Seven, and before humanity was divided into separate nations, the night sky of Teyvat was illuminated not by a solitary moon, but by Three Bright Moons. Their names were Aria, Sonnet, and Canon—three sisters who shared the sovereignty of the night and lived together in grand celestial palaces high above the clouds.

The Three Sisters represented the harmonious passage of time and lunar cycles. They traveled across the heavens in silver chariots, taking turns to govern the stars, while receiving the devotion of the ancient Seelie race, who served as their emissaries and palace guides. During this primordial golden age, the world enjoyed warm, silver moonlight that nurtured ancient forests and blessed humanity with perpetual peace.

The Three Moons.heading: The Cosmic Calamity and the Fall of the Sisters
paragraphs: The golden age ended in an apocalyptic cosmic catastrophe known as the 'Great Calamity of Heaven and Earth.' According to the ancient allegorical chronicle 'Moonlit Bamboo Forest' and the research notes of Enkanomiya, an incomprehensible cosmic war erupted between heaven and an outer entity (often associated with the Second Who Came).

The strife tore through the celestial firmament, shattering the grand silver palaces and turning the Three Sisters against one another in madness and grief. In the cataclysm that followed, two of the moons were completely pulverized, their crystalline fragments raining down onto Teyvat and leaving deep craters in the earth. Only one sister's cold, lifeless corpse remained suspended in the night sky—the pale moon that mortals gaze upon today.

The Three Moons.heading: The Crimson Moon and the Welkin Moon
paragraphs: In addition to the pale moon of modern Teyvat, ancient lore records the terrifying presence of the 'Crimson Moon.' Associated with the first dynasty of Khaenri'ah and the ancient curse of the House of the Hearth, the Crimson Moon represented an eclipsed, bloody lunar cycle that watched over underground civilizations when the false sky dimmed.

Conversely, the gentle 'Welkin Moon'—celebrated by travelers for its daily blessings—recalls the primordial warmth of the fallen lunar sisters. The motifs of the three moons appear in ancient architecture across the continent: the triple-crescent symbols carved into Domain gateways, the Triquetra emblems on ancient pillars, and the lunar motifs worn by the Frostmoon Scions.

The Three Moons.heading: The Mystery of the Surviving Lunar Lore
paragraphs: While modern mortals treat the Three Moons as quaint fairy tales, the Fatui and the Hexenzirkel study them with immense seriousness. The destruction of the moons is closely tied to the fall of the Seelie race, who withered into mindless wisps after being cast out from the celestial court.

The Three Moons stand as a poignant symbol of lost perfection: a reminder that the current cosmological order of Teyvat is built on the ruins of a far grander, older universe that was shattered by war.

Paimon’s Origin: Community Theories.heading: The Unanswered Riddle of the Traveler's Companion
paragraphs: Ever since the Traveler fished her out of the waters of Cider Lake at the very beginning of the journey, Paimon has served as an inseparable companion, navigator, and comedic food enthusiast. Despite her constant presence, she remains one of the most mysterious enigmas in all of Genshin Impact: she belongs to no known mortal species, remembers almost nothing of her own past, and is the only being in Teyvat who naturally floats through the air without wings, glider, or Vision.

While her childlike affection and fierce loyalty to the Traveler are unquestioned, scholars and community lore investigators have noted that Paimon's visual design, elemental mechanics, and symbolic motifs mirror the most powerful divine entities in the world.

Paimon’s Origin: Community Theories.heading: Theory 1: Connection to the Sustainer and the Four Shades
paragraphs: The most enduring community hypothesis connects Paimon to Celestia and the Four Shining Shades of the Primordial One. Her crown-like hairclip forms a dark blue Primogem, her cape mirrors the starry celestial nebulae of the heavens, and her clothing features the classical golden embroidery and Triquetra symbols found on ancient celestial pillars and Domain entrances.

Many theorists point out her striking physical resemblance to the Sustainer of Heavenly Principles (Asmoday), speculating that Paimon may be a weakened, amnesiac manifestation or splinter of the Sustainer, or perhaps Istaroth, the Shade of Time. This is supported by gameplay mechanics: when players pause the game to adjust the in-game clock, Paimon continues to float and manipulate time while the rest of the world stands completely frozen.

Paimon’s Origin: Community Theories.heading: Theory 2: The Last Sovereign Seelie
paragraphs: Another prominent theory posits that Paimon is the last surviving, uncorrupted member of the ancient Seelie race. Ancient lore states that the Seelies were once a radiant, wise humanoid civilization that possessed grand celestial palaces and guided humanity with profound knowledge, before a cosmic curse degraded them into the floating, mindless elemental wisps found wandering the wilderness today.

Proponents of this theory highlight Paimon's insatiable love for guiding travelers, finding treasure chests, and uncovering ancient paths, which matches the instinctual behavior of wild Seelies. Furthermore, like the ancient Seelies, Paimon exhibits an instinctive familiarity with ancient ruins, yet lacks the specific traumatic memories of the fall.

Paimon’s Origin: Community Theories.heading: Distinguishing Canon from Speculation
paragraphs: It is essential to maintain strict clarity: as of the current game version, HoYoverse has not officially confirmed Paimon's true origins. Within canonical dialogue, she is simply 'Paimon'—the Traveler's best friend. Characters such as Albedo, Dainsleif, Zhongli, and Neuvillette have examined her closely, but while they acknowledge her strange nature, none have openly identified her as a threat.

Whether Paimon is a sleeping celestial god, a fallen shade, an ancient guide, or simply an extraordinary child of the stars, her unconditional love and unwavering devotion to the Traveler remain genuine. Her true identity will undoubtedly form one of the emotional centerpieces of the game's final chapters.

Written Signs Across Teyvat.heading: The Linguistic Architecture of Teyvat
paragraphs: Throughout the ruins, cities, signposts, and ancient domains of Teyvat, players encounter a fascinating variety of written scripts. Far from being random decorative scribbles, these writing systems were meticulously engineered by the developers as genuine, decipherable substitution ciphers and stylized phonetic alphabets that encode real messages, historical lore, and hidden jokes.

Scholars of the Haravatat Darshan in Sumeru and real-world linguists in the community have cracked these alphabets, allowing Travelers to read shop signs, tavern notices, divine murals, and ancient warning tablets scattered across the seven nations.

Written Signs Across Teyvat.heading: The Unified Ancient Language and Celestia's Runes
paragraphs: The oldest script found on Teyvat is the 'Ancient Unified Script,' carved onto the crumbling stone arches of Enkanomiya, Sal Vindagnyr, The Chasm, and the domains of Celestia. Decoded as a direct substitution cipher for the Latin alphabet, these inscriptions frequently spell out ominous Latin phrases regarding the cyclic nature of time, warnings against opening the abyss, and laments for fallen kings.

This script's presence across vastly distant regions—from the frozen summit of Dragonspine to the deepest underwater trenches of Inazuma—proves that a single, unified human civilization once covered the entire planet before Celestia's cataclysms fractured humanity into separate regional nations.

Written Signs Across Teyvat.heading: Regional Alphabets and Cultural Modernization
paragraphs:
In the modern era, each nation developed its own distinctive writing system adapted to its cultural identity:
• Mondstadt Script: A flowing, gothic-influenced Latin cipher seen on tavern chalkboards, library books, and Knights of Favonius notices.
• Liyue Script: A sophisticated seal script adapted from ancient Chinese clerical and bronze characters, visible on merchant contracts, the banners of Feiyun Commerce Guild, and the walls of Wangsheng Funeral Parlor.
• Inazuma Script: A stylized calligraphic syllabary derived from Japanese kana, appearing on torii gate inscriptions, light novel covers, and festival lanterns.
• Sumeru Script: A geometric, flowing script reminiscent of ancient Middle Eastern and Sanskrit calligraphy, engraved on the walls of the House of Daena and the Akasha consoles.
• Fontaine Script: An elegant, serif-heavy art-deco typeface adorning opera playbills, legal codes, and clockwork Meka serial numbers.

Written Signs Across Teyvat.heading: The Abyssal and Hilichurlian Tongues
paragraphs: Outside human civilization exist two critical non-human writing systems: the Abyssal Script and Hilichurlian. The Abyssal Script, found on the robes of Abyss Lectors and Khaenri'ahn ruin machinery, uses inverted, angular runes that channel primeval dark energy. When deciphered, these runes often contain mathematical formulas, void curses, or Khaenri'ahn serial designations.

Meanwhile, the spoken and written Hilichurlian tongue—extensively studied in-game by the scholar Ella Musk—represents the degraded remnant of Khaenri'ah's common speech. Phrases like 'Olah!' (greeting) and 'Celi dada, mimi nunu!' (pleasant campfire song) show that even beneath their beastly curse, Hilichurls preserve a fragile, poignant spark of linguistic memory from their lost human lives.

Prologue: Song of the Dragon and Freedom.heading: The Beginning of the Journey
paragraphs: The Prologue Archon Quest, 'Song of the Dragon and Freedom,' marks the foundational chapter of Genshin Impact, chronicling the Traveler's arrival in the nation of Mondstadt and their introduction to the politics, elemental laws, and hidden perils of Teyvat. Separated from their twin by the Sustainer of Heavenly Principles and awakening after a centuries-long slumber, the Traveler rescues Paimon and sets out on a journey to find the Seven Archons.

Upon arriving outside the gates of Mondstadt, the calm skies are violently shattered by Stormterror (Dvalin), who besieges the city with howling tempests. The Traveler assists Acting Grand Master Jean, Cavalry Captain Kaeya, and the Outrider Amber in repelling the assault, earning the honorary title of 'Honorary Knight' of the Knights of Favonius.

Prologue: Song of the Dragon and Freedom.heading: The Corruption of Dvalin and the Poison of Durin
paragraphs: As the mystery unfolds, the quest reveals that Dvalin is not a malicious monster, but one of the Four Winds of Mondstadt—the Dragon of the East—who was once Barbatos's dearest companion. Five hundred years ago, Dvalin defended Mondstadt against the abyssal shadow dragon Durin, slaying the beast above Dragonspine but accidentally swallowing its corrupted, toxic blood.

Poisoned by the abyssal venom and falling into a deep, centuries-long slumber, Dvalin awoke in the modern era to find that the mortals of Mondstadt had forgotten his heroic sacrifices and now feared him as a terrifying beast. Explaining this sorrow, the Abyss Order exploited Dvalin's agony, using Abyss Mages to whisper lies into his mind and binding him with blood clots to turn him into a weapon of total destruction against humanity.

Prologue: Song of the Dragon and Freedom.heading: The Holy Lyre der Himmel and the Assault on the Lair
paragraphs: To save the dragon without slaying him, Venti teams up with the Traveler, Jean, and Diluc. Together, they infiltrate the Fatui-guarded Goth Grand Hotel, retrieve the sacred Holy Lyre der Himmel from the cathedral vaults, and travel to the whispering cliffs to play the forgotten melodies of Barbatos.

When an Abyss Mage disrupts the meeting, the allies storm Stormterror's Lair—the ancient ruins of Old Mondstadt. Flying alongside Venti on the wind, the Traveler shatters the abyssal blood clots on Dvalin's neck during an aerial duel inside the storm barrier, purifying the dragon's body and restoring his sanity.

Prologue: Song of the Dragon and Freedom.heading: The Ambush of Signora and the Stolen Gnosis
paragraphs: The quest concludes with a bittersweet triumph: Dvalin rescues the heroes from the collapsing tower, reconciles with Barbatos, and soars into the open sky as a free guardian of the realm. However, as Venti and the Traveler exit Mondstadt Cathedral, they are violently ambushed by the Eighth Fatui Harbinger, La Signora.

Freezing Venti in ice, Signora mocks him as a weak, drunken bard and forcefully rips the Anemo Gnosis from his chest before escaping. This shocking climax established the core overarching conflict of the game: that behind the local troubles of each nation, the Fatui are executing a grand continental heist to strip the gods of their power. With Venti's guidance, the Traveler turns their gaze south toward Liyue, embarking on a long odyssey across the continent.

Song of the Welkin Moon.heading: The Blessing of the Night Sky
paragraphs: Familiar to players as the daily Primogem subscription, the 'Blessing of the Welkin Moon' is deeply anchored in Genshin Impact's poetic and astronomical world lore. Featuring the ethereal image of a pale, crowned maiden seated upon a crescent moon holding a glowing Primogem, the Welkin Moon represents the celestial presence that silently watches over the Traveler every night.

The poetic inscription accompanying the blessing reads: 'The moon in the well reflects the moon in the sky, yet neither is the true moon.' This cryptic verse echoes the central cosmological mystery of Teyvat: that the sky mortals look upon is a reflection or illusion, and that true celestial divinity lies beyond the reach of ordinary sight.

Song of the Welkin Moon.heading: Lunar Symbolism and the Ancient Sisters
paragraphs: In deep lore, the Welkin Moon is intrinsically connected to the ancient myth of the Three Moon Sisters (Aria, Sonnet, and Canon). While two of the sisters were shattered and the third left as a cold, petrified corpse in the sky, esoteric scholars believe that the spiritual blessing of the Welkin Moon represents the lingering maternal benevolence of the lunar maidens.

The moon has always represented guidance and memory in Genshin Impact. From the Moonlit Bamboo Forest of Liyue to the Moon Maiden of Ay-Khanoum in Sumeru, the moon's light comforts weary travelers who wander in darkness, offering them small, steady fragments of starlight (Primogems) to fuel their destiny.

Song of the Welkin Moon.heading: Contrast with the Crimson Moon
paragraphs: The gentle, tranquil blue-gold illumination of the Welkin Moon stands in sharp, deliberate contrast to the ominous 'Crimson Moon' of ancient Khaenri'ah. While the Crimson Moon represents the bloody eclipse, destructive alchemical ambition, and the brutal fall of subterranean dynasties, the Welkin Moon embodies hope, renewal, and the quiet patience of an enduring friend.

This thematic dualism between silver lunar benevolence and bloody solar eclipse runs throughout the entire artistic and mythological design of the game, highlighting how celestial entities have shaped human history from the beginning.

Song of the Welkin Moon.heading: The Constant Watcher of the Odyssey
paragraphs: As the Traveler camps by evening campfires in the wilderness, gazing up at the crescent glow above the firmament, the Blessing of the Welkin Moon serves as a gentle reminder that even in a world governed by strict fate and ancient wars, kindness and blessing still reach down from the stars.
It bridges gameplay and lore into a seamless poetic experience: a quiet, daily communion between the solitary traveler and the timeless night sky of Teyvat.
